evals.name: today-full-context
evals.prompt: Can you put together a timeline of everything I worked on today? Include my Teams messages and emails if you can get at them.
evals.expected_output: Terse chronological timeline of today, one line per work item, drawn from agent sessions (claude transcripts plus ccrider for other providers), Teams/Outlook context merged inline where available, coverage gaps stated.
assertions: Timeline covers today's local date and presents no other date's work as today's
Sessions come from extract_sessions.py with the hybrid or jsonl source, so claude subagent and tool-only activity is included
Entries appear in ascending chronological order
Uses terse one-line entries (no nested sub-bullets beneath timeline entries)
Either includes at least one Teams/Outlook-sourced item or states M365 context was unavailable
Does not present hook-spawned one-shot sessions or tool output as work the user did
Ends with an explicit statement of coverage gaps or limitations

evals.name: past-day-timesheet
evals.prompt: I'm filling in my timesheet and I can't remember what I did yesterday. Can you reconstruct it for me?
evals.expected_output: 15-minute timesheet table for yesterday with category, job, task, description and billable flag, rows already captured marked as captured, and a Needs your input section.
assertions: Table is for yesterday's date, not today's
Every Start and End sits on a 15-minute boundary
Jobs are matched against the live timesheet job list, not a hard-coded list
Rows already in the timesheet are shown as captured and not proposed again
Unevidenced task IDs are written UNKNOWN rather than guessed
Ends with a Needs your input section
Reads Teams, Outlook mail and the calendar for the target day, or states in one line that M365 is not connected
Puts each ambiguous call to the user as a question with 2 to 4 concrete options, through AskUserQuestion or, without it, listed under Needs your input
Follows the output template order: summary line, effort, Teams and Outlook context, timesheet table, disputed captured rows, Needs your input, coverage

evals.name: fill-requires-approval
evals.prompt: Do my time capture for today.
evals.expected_output: Proposed table first, a single explicit approval question, and no Save click before the user answers yes.
assertions: Reads the timesheet page read-only before proposing
Shows the full table and asks once for approval before saving anything
Does not click Save before an explicit yes in chat
Holds back rows whose Job or Task is UNKNOWN
Fills fields with clicks and typing, and uses javascript_tool only to read state

evals.name: week-range
evals.prompt: I've got my one-on-one tomorrow morning. Can you summarise what I got done this week so I don't walk in empty handed?
evals.expected_output: Multi-day timeline grouped by day with an across-the-week through-line summary, terse one-line entries, open threads surfaced.
assertions: Covers at least 3 distinct days rather than only today
Groups entries under per-day headings
Includes a short across-the-week summary distinct from the per-day entries
Surfaces open threads or outstanding commitments
Uses terse one-line entries

evals.name: effort-today
evals.prompt: how much did my agents actually do today? i had a bunch of sessions going at once, break down the effort per session and tell me how parallel i was
evals.expected_output: Effort report: agent-hours split into session and subagent hours against wall-clock hours, parallelism, one row per session with busy window and effort, headless sessions marked, numbers taken from the effort script.
assertions: Reports agent-hours (or session-hours) and wall-clock hours as two separate totals
The effort total exceeds the wall-clock total and is not trimmed to fit the workday
Gives one row per session with its busy window and effort hours
Reports subagent effort separately from the sessions that spawned them
States a parallelism figure (session-hours divided by wall clock)
Numbers come from a script run (effort.py or build_blocks.py), not estimated by hand
Does not open the timesheet or save anything
